newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: CRICKET-India the final test for Vettori - Dykes.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-India the final test for Vettori - Dykes.

text.p: AUCKLAND, April 3 - New Zealand's cricket tour to India next month will be the final test of Daniel Vettori's authenticity as a spin bowler, chairman of selectors Ross Dykes said on Thursday.
New Zealand will play in India's Independence Cup quadrangular tournament, which also includes cricket's Asian giants Pakistan and world one-day champions Sri Lanka.
All three Asian countries are well versed in playing against spinners on tracks that suit slow bowlers.
Dykes said the tournament provided the ideal platform for Vettori to present his credentials to the cricket world.
"I think it is fair to say this will be the Daniel's biggest test ahead of going to Australia next summer," Dykes told NZPA.
"It is always a tough task for any spinner to bowl well there and this is going to be an interesting time for Daniel."
He is confident though that the teenager will handle the conditions well in India.
"We think Daniel has the potential and ability to do well and we are confident he will acquit himself well over there," Dykes said.

While the Northern Districts youngster performed well in the 2-0 test series win over Sri Lanka, his attack style was somewhat collared by the World Champions' big hitting batsmen Sanath Jayasuriya, Romesh Kaluwitharana and Aravinda de Silva.
"I think having already had a look at the Sri Lankans will give him confidence when he looks at playing the Indians and Pakistanis," said Dykes.
"The tracks over there are also likely to be more conducive to spin bowling so he'll have an interesting time."
The one factor likely to favour Vettori is that his mentor Dipak Patel may be going on his final trip for New Zealand.
Patel is familiar with the conditions and grounds in India and will be able to pass on valuable tips to the youngster.
New Zealand are to play Pakistan in either New Delhi or Cochin on May 9, India in Bangalore on May 14 and Sri Lanka in Hyderabad on May 20.
The 14-man New Zealand team was scheduled to be announced later today.
